title: rate-engine-weighted-priority-starvation-during-bulk-tenant-migration
creator: Diego Martinez
description: During a scheduled bulk tenant migration (shard rebalance) we observed a subset of tenants enter long-lived soft-throttles despite no change in their request patterns. Early investigation shows the rate engine's weighted-priority allocator temporarily computed near-zero effective allocations for affected tenant keys, causing sustained enforcement until a manual intervention (rollback) completed. This ticket tracks root cause analysis, remediation, and test coverage to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: Provision two shards with existing tenant set A (1k tenants) and target shard B.
Trigger bulk tenant migration using shard-rebalancer with parallel move batch size 200.
Run synthetic steady-state traffic generator (1 QPS per tenant key) against all tenants during migration.
Observe enforcement metrics and per-tenant effective_allocation metric in console dashboard for duration of migration.
Verify that affected tenants see sustained 429s while others remain within quota.
root_cause_summary: A normalization/rounding bug in the weighted-priority allocator combined with an unprotected fast-path for allocation recomputation during high-volume tenant move batches. When many priorities change simultaneously, the normalization used 32-bit float math and an integer-floor step that produced zero effective allocation for low-priority tenants. Additionally, a race between lease-update handler and allocation snapshotting allowed stale totals to be used, amplifying the effect.
action_items: Patch allocator: switch normalization to 64-bit double, apply conservative min_allocation clamp (epsilon) to avoid zeroing small weights.
Add atomic allocation snapshot for lease-update path so recompute uses consistent totals.
Introduce integration test that simulates bulk migration with 1k tenants and asserts no tenant allocation falls below 0.5% of fair share.
Add per-tenant allocation histogram to console and set alert if min allocation < 0.1% for >5m.
Prepare hotfix config to limit parallel move batch size to 25 until runtime patch is deployed.
progress_updates: 2025-09-18: Initial customer report and metric spike observed; on-call triaged and rolled back migration progress to stop further tenant moves.
2025-09-19: Reproducer implemented (load generator + migration tool) by @aishar; confirmed deterministic repro in staging.
2025-09-20: Allocation patch prototype submitted: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345; local unit tests added.
2025-09-22: Canary run in staging with modified allocator shows no zeroed allocations across 3 migrations; extended run to 24h.
2025-09-24: PR in review, found a concurrency gap in lease-update path; added atomic snapshot change and updated PR to github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345/files#diff-...
2025-09-25: Hotfix deployed: migration batch size limited via feature flag; monitoring alerts configured. Awaiting final merge and runtime-1.24 release window.
mitigation: Immediate mitigation applied: restricted parallel tenant move batch_size to 25 via feature flag in shard-rebalancer and rolled back in-flight large migrations. Ops configured temporary alert to detect any tenant with effective_allocation==0 for >1m and auto-pause migration for that tenant group.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover float-to-double migration for normalization function and min_allocation clamp behavior.
Integration test reproducer fails to create any tenant with effective_allocation < 0.5% under bulk migration scenario.
Canary in staging runs for 48h with no 429 spike attributable to allocator; metrics dashboard added in console.
PR merged and runtime-1.24 contains allocator fix; rollout plan and rollback tested.
Post-deploy monitoring alerting and runbook updated for migration operator.
